sub.hard_core: A batched NKI kernel stepping 10,000 tiny recurrent minds per tick with database-to-device sync. Real systems work, but the math is one batched matmul and the minds have no training objective.

Without a learning objective the NPCs do nothing interesting, and a GPU runs the same batched GEMM trivially, so the Trainium angle is not load-bearing. sub.hard_core: Attack-path search over a segmented network graph. Real logic, but a graph search does it better than an LLM agent.

ideas.take: Attack-path analysis is a graph problem BloodHound has solved for years; an LLM red-teamer on a synthetic map with a Clash skin adds no core.
ideas.reasoning: Finding which wall the attacker walked around is path search over a graph with edge preconditions, which BloodHound already does on real Active Directory data. An LLM raiding the map is slower and less complete than a search. The stronger version would compute the optimal wall placement (a min-cut) and grade players against it, but that is a training toy, and 'your real network map' will not be real at a hackathon.
ideas.red_flag: The AI does what a graph algorithm does better, on a synthetic network.

evidence.title: SpecterOps: BloodHound Community Edition

pivots.name: Fire Drill: Proving Ground
pivots.pitch: An adaptive attacker searches for social-engineering chains (voice, email, invoice) against your money-moving agent, and the fix is a deterministic provenance policy at the tool boundary, proven on a breach-versus-utility table over 200 generated held-out attacks.
pivots.change: Three changes. (1) The fix is no longer Claude Code editing a prompt: a tool-boundary proxy tags every value with its source (vendor master, trusted user, or untrusted channel such as a call transcript, email or invoice text) and blocks any money-moving call whose payee or bank fields trace to untrusted text unless an out-of-band confirmation fires; Claude proposes the policy and the engine enforces it. (2) The attacker becomes a search: Claude expands a tree of concession chains per tactic and channel, prunes branches the victim resists, and keeps winning chains as a regression suite. (3) Every claim is a number: breach rate with a confidence interval and benign-task completion before and after, on held-out variants generated from tactic x channel x wording templates the policy never saw. Voice stays as one channel for the live judge call.
pivots.why: It removes the tautology in the original: enforcement does not depend on wording, so 'what if they reword it?' is answered by design, and the utility column proves you did not just delete the tool. Each part does what it is good at: the LLM searches for attacks (a script cannot), and the engine enforces (an LLM should not). It is CaMeL's information-flow idea turned into a product for finance agents, with a measured result instead of a demo-only PASS.
pivots.label: Real system

sub.components: Victim AP agent on Claude Agent SDK (API), tree-search attacker over tactic x channel (original loop plus prompt), Cartesia Line voice channel (API), provenance-tagging tool proxy and policy engine (original), Claude policy proposer (prompt), held-out variant generator plus breach/utility harness (original), Visa sandbox payment (API), scorecard (glue/UI)
sub.hard_core: Deterministic provenance enforcement on money-moving tool arguments, plus a statistical breach-versus-utility evaluation over generated held-out attacks.

pivots.name: Parity Proxy
pivots.pitch: An MCP browsing proxy that renders each page in a real browser, computes the text a human can actually perceive, hands the agent only that layer, and logs every hidden delta as evidence.
pivots.change: Moves from accusing merchants (which needs real cheaters to exist within 36 hours) to a defensive firewall that works on every page. The core becomes a perceptual-visibility engine: computed styles, contrast against the background, font size, clipped and off-viewport boxes, occlusion via point sampling, aria-hidden and zero-opacity text. The paired human/agent crawl stays as a background measurement study rather than the demo, and Claude only classifies borderline deltas.
pivots.why: The hard core is now original engineering that is not one API call, and it is measurable: precision and recall per hiding technique on a labeled corpus. The live moment is not staged, because a judge can paste any hiding trick into a page and watch it stripped before the agent reads it. Say the limit out loud: it stops hidden instructions, not visible ones.
pivots.label: Real system

sub.components: Bright Data Scraping Browser or Playwright rendering (API), perceptual-visibility engine over computed style, layout and pixel sampling (original), DOM-text versus perceivable-text delta (original), Claude borderline classifier (prompt), MCP fetch server (glue), Elastic findings index (API), paired-identity crawl study (original, background)
sub.hard_core: Computing the human-perceivable text layer of a rendered page and diffing it against what the agent would otherwise ingest.

pivots.name: Refactor Insurance
pivots.pitch: For PRs declared 'no behavior change' (refactors, dependency bumps, agent-written cleanups), a swarm of Claude hunters tries to write a test that passes on main and fails on the PR; any such test is machine-checked proof of a regression and blocks the merge.
pivots.change: Fixes the unsound oracle: restricting to declared no-behavior-change PRs makes a differential test (green on base, red on head, stable over five reruns) an objective proof with no argument about intent. The staking market is dropped, or kept only as an optional x402 bounty. Hunters are scored on a mutation benchmark of seeded regressions, so the pitch ends on a catch rate.
pivots.why: The AI does the hard reasoning (finding an input that exposes a subtle behavior change) and a script does the judging, which is exactly the split the Anthropic judge looks for. The verdict is mechanically verifiable, the catch rate on seeded mutants is a number, and it targets a real, growing workload: the flood of agent-written refactor PRs.
pivots.label: Real system

sub.components: Claude/Factory Droid hunter agents writing differential tests (API plus prompt), sandboxed base-versus-head test runner with flake filter (original), mutation-injection benchmark for catch rate (original), GitHub check gate and report (glue), Greptile context for hunters (API), optional x402 bounty (API)
sub.hard_core: A differential-testing oracle (passes on base, fails on head, stable across reruns) that turns an LLM's bug hunt into machine-verified proof, measured by catch rate on seeded regressions.

picks.why: After the pivot it is the deepest security build in the pool: a deterministic policy engine and a measured breach-versus-utility table, with the live judge phone call kept as the hook.
The most real system as written: an LP, invariants and a two-phase commit move the money, so it survives every 'where does the AI touch the money?' question.
An original engine (lineage graph, bisect, cascade rollback) for a documented, unsolved problem, with a crisp poison, bisect, rollback demo.
Ground-truth settlement in reducers plus a service-rate constraint makes it a measurable security-versus-utility system rather than a jailbreak toy.
A clean, verifiable oracle where Claude does the hard reasoning and a test runner does the judging; small enough to finish and polish.

ceo_note: Strip the jargon and more than half the pool is sponsor APIs chained to a prompt, and several ideas (AgentFICO, Stump Market, Kernel Swarm, Flytrap, Coyote Time, Save States) already exist as products or as a sponsor's own feature. Only Netting House, Memory Blame and Vault Heist have an engine of their own as written; Fire Drill becomes the strongest once its fix is a deterministic policy engine with a measured breach-versus-utility table, not Claude patching a prompt it wrote. Whatever you build, make the thing that decides the outcome (moves money, blocks a call, settles a coin) code you wrote and can verify, with Claude doing the reasoning around it.
